sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and page setup
sections.what: Brings in the tools the page needs: the industry data, the sign-in check, the data fetching tools, the icons, the lifecycle formatter, the project totals helper and the citation helpers.
sections.why: Likely reason: the page draws on several shared pieces, so each is imported at the top.
sections.watch_out: The page depends on many shared modules, so a renamed export in any of them will break this file.

sections.name: IndustryHeader
sections.title: Top bar with navigation and user info
sections.what: Draws the sticky top bar on each industry page. It shows the CPD home link, a breadcrumb back to the industry list, the current industry name, the signed-in user's name and role, and a sign-out button.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps navigation and the signed-in identity visible while the reader scrolls.
sections.watch_out: The name and role come from the auth context, so if no user is loaded the role shows as empty brackets.

sections.name: SourceTypeIcon
sections.title: Icon for each source type
sections.what: Shows a small icon that matches a source's kind, such as a building for an industry association or a flask for a consulting firm. Unknown kinds fall back to the building icon.
sections.why: Lets readers tell source kinds apart at a glance.
sections.watch_out: A new source type added to the data but missing from the icon map silently gets the fallback icon.

sections.name: AuthorityBadge
sections.title: Small label showing authority tier
sections.what: Shows a short label such as T1, T2 or T3 with a matching colour. Tier 1 is the most authoritative (regulators and lead associations), and tier 3 is trade press.
sections.why: Shows readers how much weight a source carries.
sections.watch_out: The tier number is trusted as given, so the badge does not check that it is 1, 2 or 3.

sections.name: DrawerState
sections.title: Stored details for the open evidence panel
sections.what: Holds what the evidence panel needs: the node name, its path from the top of the tree, and its list of citations. When no panel is open, this value is empty.
sections.why: Keeps the panel's content in one place so it can be opened and closed.
sections.watch_out: Citations are copied in when the panel opens, so the list does not refresh while the panel is showing.

sections.name: EvidenceDrawer (part 1)
sections.title: Evidence panel frame and close handling
sections.what: Draws the right-side panel that lists the sources behind one taxonomy node. It closes when the reader clicks the dark backdrop, clicks the close button, or presses Escape. If there are no citations it shows a short message saying so.
sections.why: Lets readers check the evidence without leaving the page.
sections.watch_out: The Escape key listener is attached to the whole window, so it must be removed when the panel closes or it keeps firing.

sections.name: EvidenceDrawer (part 2)
sections.title: Citation cards and unresolved citation warnings
sections.what: Shows one card per citation. If a citation points to a document or source that is not registered, it shows a warning card with the quote instead of hiding it.
sections.why: Likely reason: a missing registry entry should be visible, not silently dropped, so gaps in traceability show up.
sections.watch_out: Warning cards show the excerpt but no source name, so the fix belongs in the registry, not the card.

sections.name: EvidenceDrawer (part 3)
sections.title: Citation details, quote type and jump link
sections.what: Fills each card with the source name, authority tier, publisher, document title, year and section. It shows whether the quote is verbatim, paraphrased or a summary, plus the quote text, any note, and a Jump to source link when a web address exists.
sections.why: Lets readers check each claim against the original publisher.
sections.watch_out: The external link opens in a new tab, and a missing or broken web address simply hides the link.

sections.name: EvidenceDrawer (part 4)
sections.title: Footer explaining quote labels
sections.what: Shows a fixed footer at the bottom of the panel that explains the three quote labels and the three authority tiers.
sections.why: Gives readers the key they need to read the labels without outside help.
sections.watch_out: The tier descriptions are typed into the text, so they must be edited by hand if the tier rules change.

sections.name: OpenDrawerFn
sections.title: Type for the open-panel callback
sections.what: Defines the shape of the function that opens the evidence panel for a node. It takes the node name and the path down to that node.
sections.why: Lets several child components share one way of opening the panel.
sections.watch_out: Changing its parameters means updating every component that passes it in.

sections.name: LeafRow
sections.title: Row for a final item with no children
sections.what: Draws one end-of-tree item with its name, an optional description, and a citation count button when sources exist. Clicking the button opens the evidence panel for that item.
sections.why: End items have nothing to expand, so they get a simpler row.
sections.watch_out: The test id is built from the name by replacing symbols, so two names that differ only by symbols could collide.

sections.name: ChildNode (part 1)
sections.title: Setup for an expandable sub-item
sections.what: Starts a mid-level tree item. If it has no children it hands off to the simple leaf row. Otherwise it remembers whether it is open, and it starts open only at the first two levels.
sections.why: Likely reason: the top levels start open so the main structure is visible without clicks.
sections.watch_out: The starting state depends on depth, so changing that rule changes what a first-time reader sees.

sections.name: ChildNode (part 2)
sections.title: Display and toggle for an expandable sub-item
sections.what: Draws an expandable sub-item with its name, a count of variants, a citation button and a description. Clicking the row or arrow opens or closes its children. The citation button opens the evidence panel without toggling the row.
sections.why: Stopping the click from spreading keeps the citation button and the row toggle separate.
sections.watch_out: The variant count uses the number of direct children only, so deeper items are not included.

sections.name: ChildNode (part 3)
sections.title: Closing end of the sub-item
sections.what: Closes the sub-item component definition. It holds no behaviour of its own.
sections.why: Structural end of the component.

sections.name: TopLevelNode (part 1)
sections.title: Top-level group header and citation button
sections.what: Draws a main group of the taxonomy with a large number, its name, a count of types, a sources button and its description. Groups start expanded, and clicking the header opens or closes them.
sections.why: Main groups are the entry points, so they start open.
sections.watch_out: The status label shows a fixed placeholder for every group rather than a real value.

sections.name: TopLevelNode (part 2)
sections.title: Children of a top-level group and toggle
sections.what: Shows the sub-items under an expanded top-level group. Groups with children show an up or down arrow that matches whether they are open.
sections.why: Likely reason: the arrow shows whether a group can open and what state it is in.
sections.watch_out: Children are always given depth 1, so their indent does not change with the group's own depth.

sections.name: TaxonomySourcesPanel
sections.title: Panel listing the taxonomy publishers
sections.what: Shows a card listing each publisher used for this industry, with its icon, short name, tier, type, country and a short description. Shows nothing when the industry has no sources.
sections.why: Lets readers see which publishers the classification is built on.
sections.watch_out: When the source list is empty the whole panel disappears with no message, so a data gap is easy to miss.

sections.name: PlantRow
sections.title: Shape of one plant record
sections.what: Describes the fields each plant carries, such as name, operator, country, technology, lifecycle stage, status, capacity and map coordinates.
sections.why: Gives the plant table a clear, consistent layout for its data.
sections.watch_out: Many fields can be empty, so any code that displays them must handle missing values.

sections.name: PlantsPanel (part 1)
sections.title: Plants panel data, sorting and citation setup
sections.what: Loads the plants for this industry, sorts them by the chosen column, and wires each cell to the full citation view. The whole panel hides itself when there are no plants.
sections.why: Hiding an empty section avoids a blank table for industries with no data.
sections.watch_out: Sorting by capacity treats a missing capacity as zero, so those plants sort as the smallest.

sections.name: PlantsPanel (part 2)
sections.title: Country chips and plant table
sections.what: Shows a chip for each country with its plant count, then a table with one row per plant. Each name links to that plant's page, and most cells can open their sources.
sections.why: Gives a quick country summary and full detail in one place.
sections.watch_out: Missing values show a placeholder, and the stage badge colour depends on the stage value, so a new stage may look unstyled.

sections.name: PlantsPanel (part 3)
sections.title: Plants panel footer note
sections.what: Closes the table and shows a note saying where the plant data comes from and pointing readers to the citation badges.
sections.why: States the sources so readers know how the list was built.
sections.watch_out: The source list is typed in as text, so it can drift from the real data.

sections.name: CoverageCard
sections.title: Coverage figures card
sections.what: Shows how many projects this industry tracks, the number of taxonomy leaves and top-level groups, and a line comparing the industry with the live reference industry. It reads live totals instead of using a fixed number.
sections.why: The code comment says counts must come from live data, never a hardcoded count or placeholder zero.
sections.watch_out: The progress bar is only full or empty, based on whether any projects exist, so it shows no partial progress.

sections.name: IndustryDetail (part 1)
sections.title: Page entry point and industry lookup
sections.what: The page for one industry, found from the slug in the web address. It shows a not-found message when the slug matches nothing, and it sets up the evidence panel state and header counts.
sections.why: Looking up the industry first means every later part can rely on it being present.
sections.watch_out: The nuclear slug redirects to the same address, so the redirect may not leave the page. Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: IndustryDetail (part 2)
sections.title: Page heading, status and under-construction notice
sections.what: Shows the industry's status badge, tagline, name and description. For industries still being built it shows a notice pointing readers to the live reference industry.
sections.why: Tells readers the data is incomplete instead of leaving them to guess.
sections.watch_out: The notice links to the first live industry, so if none is live the link is simply missing.

sections.name: IndustryDetail (part 3)
sections.title: Taxonomy tree and side panels layout
sections.what: Lays out the main taxonomy tree next to the sources list and the key metrics area. Shows counts of stages, leaf types and total nodes, plus any taxonomy notes.
sections.why: Puts the classification in the main column and supporting information beside it.
sections.watch_out: The layout switches between one and three columns at set screen widths, so changes to those classes change the look on each screen size.

sections.name: IndustryDetail (part 4)
sections.title: Key metrics, coverage and switch links
sections.what: Lists the industry's key metrics, but every value shows a placeholder, not a number. Then it shows the coverage card and a grid linking to up to twelve other industries.
sections.why: Likely reason: the metric values are not connected to data yet, so the page marks them as unavailable.
sections.watch_out: Readers may take the metric labels as having data, but every one shows a placeholder until real values are wired in.

summary: Detail page for a single industry, showing its structure, sources and projects. Only the imports at the top of the file were visible.
purpose: Likely reason: gives a visitor one industry's details in one place. The visible code does not confirm the full purpose.
why: Reason not stated in the code, beyond the imports showing it reads industry data, citations and project totals.
how: 1. Loads the industry data and its taxonomy sources from the shared industry module. 2. Uses the signed-in user and citation helpers. 3. Formats lifecycle stages and project totals. The rest of the file was not visible, so the steps after this are unknown.
inputs: The industry code from the web address, the shared industry data, the signed-in user and the citation and total helpers.
outputs: Not visible in the code shown.
risks: Only the imports were visible, so no risks in the logic can be judged. Several imports come from the shared industry module, so a change there affects this page.
debug: If the page fails to load, check that the industry code exists in the shared list and that the imports resolve. The rest of the file was not provided, so check the rendering code directly.
